sentences.en: But as for our topic today, we're going to talk about confidence and what it is about confident people that
sentences.zh: 至于我们今天的主题，我们要聊聊自信，聊聊自信的人身上究竟有什么特质

sentences.en: is so alluring, so fabulous, and how we can emulate it, how we can cultivate this brilliant, bright, amazing attitude.

sentences.en: So let's begin by dismantling this core assumption or core misconception, I should say, that confidence is a fixed personal attribute.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们先来拆解这个核心假设，或者说核心误区：自信是一种固定的个人属性。

sentences.en: You either have it or you don't.
sentences.zh: 你要么有，要么没有。

sentences.en: Is that true or not?
sentences.zh: 这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: I'm going to give you the answer right now, and then I'm going to give you the explanation.
sentences.zh: 我现在就给你答案，然后再给出解释。

sentences.en: The answer is no, it's not.
sentences.zh: 答案是：不，并非如此。

sentences.en: According to research, including a really comprehensive study on the heritability of confidence conducted in 2021, confidence is only between 9% to 28% heritable.
sentences.zh: 根据研究，包括2021年进行的一项关于自信遗传性的非常全面的研究，自信的遗传率仅在9%到28%之间。

sentences.en: What that means, if you don't understand genetics, because sometimes I barely do, is that the majority
sentences.zh: 如果你不懂遗传学（因为有时连我自己也搞不太懂），这意味着我们自信的绝大部分，

sentences.en: of our confidence somewhere between 72% and 91% is shaped by things like environment, experiences,
sentences.zh: 大约72%到91%，是由环境、经历、

sentences.en: mindset, choices, not just your genetics, not just things that feel outside of your orbit of control.
sentences.zh: 心态、选择等因素塑造的，而不仅仅是你的基因，不仅仅是那些感觉超出你控制范围的事情。

sentences.en: For the most part, something like confidence is something that we can change.
sentences.zh: 在很大程度上，自信是可以改变的。

sentences.en: We can kind of intercept and form to our desires.
sentences.zh: 我们可以干预它，并将其塑造成我们想要的样子。

sentences.en: And to truly understand why this is the case, and to truly understand like the foundation of confidence, you have to understand one of its core ingredients, which is self-efficacy.
sentences.zh: 要真正理解为什么会这样，并真正理解自信的基础，你必须理解它的核心成分之一：自我效能感。

sentences.en: Self-efficacy is a concept that was first named or labeled, I guess, by someone called Albert Bondura, a very famous social psychologist who we talk about a lot.
sentences.zh: 自我效能感这个概念最初是由Albert Bandura命名或定义的，他是一位我们经常提到的非常著名的社会心理学家。

sentences.en: And it is basically our belief in our capacity to execute the behaviors necessary to produce specific performance attainments.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是指我们对自己执行必要行为以产生特定表现结果的能力的信念。

sentences.en: In simpler terms, because that is such a convoluted definition, it is your belief that you can successfully perform a given task, you can achieve
sentences.zh: 用更简单的话来说（因为那个定义太晦涩了），它就是你相信自己能够成功完成某项任务，能够实现

sentences.en: a particular goal, you can, I guess, present yourself a specific way based on your intentions and your desires.
sentences.zh: 某个特定目标，能够根据你的意图和愿望以某种方式展现自己。

sentences.en: It is not so much your belief that things will go well.
sentences.zh: 它并不完全是你相信事情会进展顺利。

sentences.en: It's not so much your belief that people will like you.
sentences.zh: 它并不完全是你相信别人会喜欢你。

sentences.en: It's not your belief in anything outside of your control.
sentences.zh: 它不是你对任何超出你控制范围的事情的信念。

sentences.en: It is belief in yourself.
sentences.zh: 它是对你自己的信念。

sentences.en: Before we can become confident, we need self-efficacy.
sentences.zh: 在我们变得自信之前，我们需要自我效能感。

sentences.en: And the great thing about self-efficacy is that it can only be built and earned.
sentences.zh: 自我效能感最棒的一点是，它只能通过积累和赢得。

sentences.en: It cannot just be granted to us.
sentences.zh: 它不能被直接赋予我们。

sentences.en: It is not either there or not the moment we are born.
sentences.zh: 它不是我们出生时就自带的。

sentences.en: So there are four primary sources through which self-efficacy is developed and strengthened.
sentences.zh: 因此，自我效能感的发展和增强主要有四个来源。

sentences.en: When you understand these sources, you kind of precisely know how confidence is built in someone brick by brick through the process of learning and environment and experiences.
sentences.zh: 当你理解了这些来源，你就能精准地知道自信是如何通过学习、环境和经历的过程，在一个人身上一点一滴建立起来的。

sentences.en: So the first source, the very first one is something called mastery experiences or inactive attainments.
sentences.zh: 第一个来源，也是最基础的一个，叫做“掌控体验”或“行为成就”。

sentences.en: Basically, when you successfully perform a task, especially one that you initially found rather challenging, it creates a belief in your capabilities.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，当你成功完成一项任务时，尤其是那些你最初觉得相当具有挑战性的任务，它会建立起你对自己能力的信念。

sentences.en: This starts like as like from like three months old.
sentences.zh: 这从三个月大时就开始了。

sentences.en: Let's use the example of learning how to ride a bike because it's a very good one.
sentences.zh: 让我们以学习骑自行车为例，因为它是一个非常好的例子。

sentences.en: You know, riding a bike is kind of scary.
sentences.zh: 你知道，骑自行车有点吓人。

sentences.en: Like it is kind of scary.
sentences.zh: 它确实有点吓人。

sentences.en: Like you have to balance on these two wheels and you can go really, really fast and you'll probably fall off.
sentences.zh: 你必须在两个轮子上保持平衡，而且速度可能会很快，你很可能会摔倒。

sentences.en: You know, the first few attempts involve wobbling and falling and that erodes your confidence.
sentences.zh: 你知道，最初的几次尝试涉及摇晃和摔倒，这会削弱你的自信。

sentences.en: But with each kind of like successful pedal stroke, each moment of balance, like your belief and your ability to ride independently grows stronger.
sentences.zh: 但随着每一次成功的踩踏，每一次保持平衡的瞬间，你独立骑行的能力信念就会变得更强。

sentences.en: It's all based on these moments of feeling like I didn't believe I could do this, but I can.
sentences.zh: 这一切都基于那些“我原以为我做不到，但我做到了”的瞬间。

sentences.en: And that for our mind kind of acts as these concrete data points that rewire your internal narrative.
sentences.zh: 对于我们的大脑来说，这些瞬间就像是重塑你内心叙事的具体数据点。

sentences.en: It rewires your trust in your own abilities.
sentences.zh: 它重塑了你对自己能力的信任。

sentences.en: The fact that you've kind of, you are capable.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，你是能够做到的。

sentences.en: Now the brain actively seeks and reinforces these positive experiences, which means that the next
sentences.zh: 现在，大脑会主动寻求并强化这些积极体验，这意味着下一次

sentences.en: time you encounter something scary or new, the judgment of others, the beginning of a new job,
sentences.zh: 当你遇到可怕或新鲜的事情时，比如他人的评判、开始一份新工作、

sentences.en: whatever it is, your brain kind of subconsciously looks back at these prior moments and goes, actually, no, like we are fully capable of managing this.
sentences.zh: 无论是什么，你的大脑都会潜意识地回顾这些过往的时刻，然后说：“其实不，我们完全有能力处理这件事。”

sentences.en: These moments of mastery can be deliberately created.
sentences.zh: 这些掌控时刻是可以被刻意创造的。

sentences.en: And that's really important because the more times you show yourself through trial and error
sentences.zh: 这一点非常重要，因为你通过试错

sentences.en: and through believing in yourself that you can do something, the more confident you will become.
sentences.zh: 以及相信自己能做成某事来向自己证明的次数越多，你就会变得越自信。

sentences.en: Next, we have vicarious experiences or social modeling.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们有“替代性体验”或“社会榜样”。

sentences.en: We are, of course, inherently social beings, and we learn a tremendous amount by simply observing others.
sentences.zh: 我们当然是天生的社会性动物，我们通过简单地观察他人就能学到很多东西。

sentences.en: When you see someone similar to yourself successfully perform a task that you want to do, it can significantly strengthen your belief that you
sentences.zh: 当你看到一个与你相似的人成功完成了你想做的事情时，这会显著增强你相信自己

sentences.en: also possess the capabilities to master similar activities.
sentences.zh: 也具备掌握类似活动的能力的信念。

sentences.en: This is why mentors, role models, even peers are so crucial in building confidence.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么导师、榜样，甚至同龄人在建立自信方面如此关键。

sentences.en: If you're, you know, a budding entrepreneur and you see someone from a similar background successfully launch their business, it sends a really powerful message.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个初出茅庐的创业者，看到一个背景相似的人成功创办了公司，这会传递出一个非常有力的信息。

sentences.en: Like if they can do it, maybe I can too.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能做到，也许我也能。

sentences.en: This actually really explains why representation matters and is so important for marginalized groups.
sentences.zh: 这其实很好地解释了为什么代表性很重要，以及为什么它对边缘化群体如此重要。

sentences.en: There was a study done in 2016 in the UK and researchers asked high achieving university students from underrepresented backgrounds to basically
sentences.zh: 英国在2016年进行了一项研究，研究人员要求来自代表性不足背景的高成就大学生，给那些

sentences.en: send letters to students from similar backgrounds who were considering university and just talk about their experience, talk about the fact that it's possible.
sentences.zh: 正在考虑上大学的相似背景的学生写信，谈谈他们的经历，谈谈这一切是可能的。

sentences.en: So there were over 11,
sentences.zh: 这项研究有超过11000人参与，

sentences.en: 11,000 people in this study and these letters were really positive.
sentences.zh: 这些信件非常积极。

sentences.en: They were like, shoot for the stars, you can do it, aim higher.
sentences.zh: 他们写道：“志存高远，你能做到，目标定高一点。”

sentences.en: And the researchers tracked students' application decisions and found that there was a significant increase in applications to more prestigious unis
sentences.zh: 研究人员追踪了学生的申请决定，发现与未收到信件的群体相比，收到信件的群体申请更负盛名大学的比例显著增加。

sentences.en: amongst the group that received the letters versus groups that did not.
sentences.zh: 所以，这并不是盲目模仿。

sentences.en: So this isn't about blind imitation.
sentences.zh: 这是关于看到他人展示出的成功路径，从而为你自己的可能性感提供参考。

sentences.en: It's about seeing a pathway to success that is demonstrated by others, which then informs your own sense of possibility.
sentences.zh: 这正是关于看到他人所展示的成功路径，从而为你自己的可能性感提供参考。

sentences.en: It's also why I think that we could do with more admiration in this society.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我认为在这个社会中，我们需要更多的赞赏。

sentences.en: Instead of being jealous of people who have what you want or have the life that you want
sentences.zh: 与其嫉妒那些拥有你想要的东西、过着你想要的生活的人，

sentences.en: or who are doing better than you, these people can act as basically proof that your dreams maybe aren't even that big enough because this person has managed to do it.
sentences.zh: 或者那些比你做得更好的人，这些人其实可以作为证明，证明你的梦想可能还不够大，因为这个人已经做到了。

sentences.en: Therefore, you can too.
sentences.zh: 因此，你也可以做到。

sentences.en: There is a pathway that is accessible.
sentences.zh: 有一条切实可行的路径。

sentences.en: So confidence can be acquired through observation in a really significant way.
sentences.zh: 所以，自信可以通过观察以一种非常显著的方式获得。

sentences.en: The third way we gain self-efficacy is through social persuasion.
sentences.zh: 我们获得自我效能感的第三种方式是通过社会说服。

sentences.en: So it's not observing someone else doing something.
sentences.zh: 这并不是观察别人做某事。

sentences.en: It's being encouraged by people who you admire.
sentences.zh: 而是受到你所钦佩的人的鼓励。

sentences.en: Having people like a coach, a parent, a teacher, a friend, someone that can say, you're doing a good job.
sentences.zh: 有教练、父母、老师、朋友这样的人，有人能对你说，你做得很好。

sentences.en: You are capable of doing this.
sentences.zh: 你有能力做到这一点。

sentences.en: Positive feedback, it's truly so motivational because we really do like external validation secretly, but also not secretly.
sentences.zh: 积极的反馈，它真的非常具有激励作用，因为我们内心深处确实喜欢外部的认可，而且这种喜欢并不隐秘。

sentences.en: And so if you have someone who you admire who was saying like, wow, you really are getting better and you're improving and you're doing well, you're actually prepared to fail more.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你有一个你钦佩的人说，哇，你真的在进步，你做得很好，你实际上就更愿意去面对失败。

sentences.en: You're prepared to fail more in some circumstances at least because you have this weird desire within you to succeed more and you kind of put yourself,
sentences.zh: 至少在某些情况下，你更愿意去面对失败，因为你内心有一种想要获得更多成功的奇怪渴望，你某种程度上让自己，

sentences.en: you kind of face opportunities more often.
sentences.zh: 你某种程度上更频繁地面对机会。

sentences.en: You put yourself in the path for success more often, even though you know that failure might be a possibility because you believe in yourself even
sentences.zh: 你更频繁地让自己走上成功的道路，即使你知道失败可能是一种可能性，因为你相信自己，即使

sentences.en: in those moments when you do fail because you have this strong sense of someone else believes in me despite missed opportunities, despite moments of ill confidence.
sentences.zh: 在那些你确实失败的时刻，因为你有一种强烈的信念，即有人相信我，尽管错失了机会，尽管有缺乏自信的时刻。

sentences.en: Therefore, I can believe in myself.
sentences.zh: 因此，我可以相信自己。

sentences.en: There's also the opposite, which is discouragement.
sentences.zh: 还有相反的情况，那就是打击。

sentences.en: Other people can really make us feel terrible about ourselves.
sentences.zh: 其他人真的会让我们对自己感觉很糟糕。

sentences.en: From parents who are dismissive to childhood bullies.
sentences.zh: 从冷漠的父母到童年的霸凌者。

sentences.en: You know, I remember I had a teacher once who was really, really mean to me and I was like, why do you have beef with me?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我记得有一次我有一位老师，对我真的非常刻薄，我当时想，你为什么对我这么有意见？

sentences.en: Like I'm literally seven years old and I felt really like, I remember feeling really bad about myself and not wanting to try and not wanting to speak up.
sentences.zh: 我当时才七岁，我真的感觉，我记得当时对自己感觉很糟糕，不想尝试，也不想开口说话。

sentences.en: Discouragement is equally as powerful as encouragement.
sentences.zh: 打击与鼓励同样具有强大的力量。

sentences.en: That is why it is so important to surround yourself with good people.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么让自己身边围绕着好人如此重要。

sentences.en: It may be hard to go up against this if you've had, you know, a family who was really awful or if you were bullied or if you do feel
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个非常糟糕的家庭，或者如果你曾经被霸凌，或者如果你确实感觉到，

sentences.en: like your environment is really what made you the way you were and it's hard to escape.
sentences.zh: 你的环境确实造就了现在的你，而且很难逃脱，那么去对抗这些可能很难。

sentences.en: But the older you get, you do have choices to be around people who will care about you, who will elevate you, who will encourage you.
sentences.zh: 但随着年龄的增长，你确实有选择权，可以选择和那些关心你、提升你、鼓励你的人在一起。

sentences.en: You know, if your friends are secretly trying to tear you down or if you are constantly listening to what people online are saying that is mean or cruel, if you let the words
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你的朋友在暗中试图拆你的台，或者如果你一直在听网上那些刻薄或残忍的言论，如果你让你的家人

sentences.en: of your family members really invade your mindset, confidence, it will be harder to obtain.
sentences.zh: 说的话真的侵蚀了你的心态，那么自信就会变得更难获得。

sentences.en: Luckily, we have one final source of self-efficacy to talk about and that's our ability to manage our own emotional reaction to stress.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我们还有最后一个关于自我效能感的来源要谈，那就是我们管理自己对压力的情绪反应的能力。

sentences.en: It's our physiological and emotional states.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的生理和情绪状态。

sentences.en: Our mood, our stress levels, that can profoundly influence how we judge our potential for success.
sentences.zh: 我们的情绪、我们的压力水平，会深刻地影响我们如何判断自己成功的潜力。

sentences.en: If you're feeling calm, energized and physically prepared for a task, you will believe in yourself more than if you went to
sentences.zh: 如果你感到平静、精力充沛，并且在身体上为一项任务做好了准备，那么你会比那些

sentences.en: bed super late or if you have had too much coffee or you're hungry.
sentences.zh: 睡得很晚，或者喝了太多咖啡，或者感到饥饿的人更相信自己。

sentences.en: These choices matter and these are choices that you have control over.
sentences.zh: 这些选择很重要，而且这些是你能够控制的选择。

sentences.en: Basically, how you approach stress, how you learn to relate to your emotions, how you physically prepare yourself is a factor in whether you feel capable.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你如何应对压力，你如何学会与自己的情绪相处，你如何从身体上准备自己，都是你是否感到有能力的因素。

sentences.en: But that also means that we can create routines and patterns and traditions that we know will make us feel confident
sentences.zh: 但这同时也意味着，我们可以创造一些我们知道会让我们感到自信的日常习惯、模式和传统，

sentences.en: and good as a way to prepare us and counteract negative emotional states that kind of come with doing new things or being in front of new people.
sentences.zh: 以此作为一种准备方式，来抵消那些伴随着做新事物或面对新人群而产生的负面情绪状态。

sentences.en: So when you understand these four sources, it becomes really clear, right, that confidence isn't an inherited trait.
sentences.zh: 所以当你理解了这四个来源，就很清楚了，对吧，自信不是一种遗传的特质。

sentences.en: If you consistently seek out opportunities for mastery, if you observe others who are successful, if you go where you are valued, if you learn how to
sentences.zh: 如果你持续寻求精进的机会，如果你观察那些成功的人，如果你去到你被重视的地方，如果你学会如何

sentences.en: manage your anxiety and your physiological state, your self-efficacy and therefore your confidence will likely grow.
sentences.zh: 管理你的焦虑和生理状态，你的自我效能感，进而你的自信心，很可能会增长。

sentences.en: It is important here to talk about the fact that although confidence isn't inherited,
sentences.zh: 这里很重要的一点是，虽然自信不是遗传的，

sentences.en: it is, you know, really quite deeply influenced by how you were raised and who you grew up around.
sentences.zh: 但它确实在很大程度上受到你的成长方式和你身边成长环境的深刻影响。

sentences.en: You know, if you, again, had parents who are deeply discouraging, if you grew up in poverty, if you grew up
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你再次拥有非常打击人的父母，如果你在贫困中长大，如果你在成长过程中，

sentences.en: with, you know, mentors or teachers or no examples of success, you are starting from a harder point.
sentences.zh: 没有导师或老师，或者没有成功的榜样，你的起点会更艰难。

sentences.en: And we have to be completely honest about that.
sentences.zh: 我们必须完全诚实地面对这一点。

sentences.en: It's not about ignoring those disadvantages.
sentences.zh: 这不是要忽视那些劣势。

sentences.en: I would not be doing my job if I sat here and said, everyone starts from zero and starts at the same starting point.
sentences.zh: 如果我坐在这里说，每个人都从零开始，起点都一样，那我就没有尽到我的职责。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: And everyone has the equal ability to build confidence because it's just not the case.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有平等的建立自信的能力，因为事实并非如此。

sentences.en: But what I'm really trying to say is that it is possible.
sentences.zh: 但我真正想说的是，这是有可能的。

sentences.en: So it's not like if you've had these experiences, you are completely doomed.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是说如果你有过这些经历，你就彻底完了。

sentences.en: If you have been raised to shrink yourself, to talk down to yourself, if you don't feel great about yourself, these are things that can actually be undone.
sentences.zh: 如果你从小被教导要缩减自己、贬低自己，如果你对自己感觉不好，这些其实是可以被扭转的。

sentences.en: They were done to you.
sentences.zh: 这些是别人对你做的。

sentences.en: That means that they have kind of like a counteracting or counterbalancing action that can also do upon you, that you can
sentences.zh: 这意味着它们有一种抵消或平衡的作用，也可以作用于你，你可以

sentences.en: do upon yourself, not to reverse those things and to reverse those experiences, but to integrate them and say that you are more than them.
sentences.zh: 对自己做，不是为了逆转那些事情和经历，而是为了整合它们，并说你比它们更强大。

sentences.en: We're going to talk a little bit more about that later on.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会更多地谈论这一点。

sentences.en: But if you want to understand how you can make yourself believe that you are confident, you have to know the name
sentences.zh: 但如果你想了解如何让自己相信自己是自信的，你必须知道卡罗尔·德韦克（Carol Dweck）这个名字。

sentences.en: Carol Dweck.
sentences.zh: 她是斯坦福大学著名的心理学家，最优秀的心理学家之一，她发现关于我们的智力和能力，

sentences.en: She is a renowned Stanford psychologist, one of the best, who discovered that there are two and
sentences.zh: 我们有两种，而且实际上只有两种基本的心态。

sentences.en: really only two fundamental mindsets we can have regarding our intelligence and our abilities.
sentences.zh: 你可能以前听说过它们。

sentences.en: You've probably heard of them before.
sentences.zh: 你可以拥有固定型心态或成长型心态。

sentences.en: You can either have a fixed or a growth mindset.
sentences.zh: 拥有固定型心态的人认为他们的基本能力、智力、自信，这些都是静态的特质。

sentences.en: Someone with a fixed mindset believes that their basic abilities, their intelligence, their confidence, these are static traits.
sentences.zh: 它们就是那样。

sentences.en: They are what they are.
sentences.zh: 他们天生如此。

sentences.en: They were born that way.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有什么办法可以改变它们。

sentences.en: There's little that can be done to change them.
sentences.zh: 如果你擅长数学，那是因为你天生就擅长数学。

sentences.en: If you're good at math, it's because you were born being good at math.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有自信，那是因为你天生就是这样。

sentences.en: If you don't have confidence, it's because that's how you were born.
sentences.zh: 没有什么可以改变的。

sentences.en: There's nothing you can change.
sentences.zh: 没有什么能改变这一点。

sentences.en: There's nothing you can do to change that.
sentences.zh: 这种观点是自愿选择的。

sentences.en: This kind of perspective is voluntary.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来很刺耳，但你确实选择了那样去相信。

sentences.en: I know it's going to sound harsh, but you do choose to believe that way.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当你面对障碍、面对挫折时，当你审视自己的自信水平并感到被它们耗尽时，

sentences.en: And so what that means is that when you face obstacles, when you face setbacks, when you look at your confidence levels and feel depleted by them,
sentences.zh: 你觉得你无法改变它们。

sentences.en: you don't feel like you can change them.
sentences.zh: 你觉得你永远都会是这样。

sentences.en: You feel like you are always going to be this way.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，拥有成长型心态的人不仅相信自己，而且相信他们最

sentences.en: In contrast, a person with a growth mindset believes in themselves, but also believes that their most
sentences.zh: 基本的能力可以通过奉献、努力、练习来发展，你的大脑、天赋、个性，这些都只是起点。

sentences.en: basic abilities can be developed through dedication and hard work and practice and your brain, talent, personality, those are just starting points.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们拥有我们所说的内部控制点。

sentences.en: In other words, they have what we call an internal locus of control.
sentences.zh: 他们相信自己有能力改变自己的行为，从而改变结果，甚至改变自己的命运。

sentences.en: They believe in their ability to change their actions and therefore an outcome, but also to change their fate.
sentences.zh: 基本上，当你相信我能行，我在扩展，我在学习，我在体验，我是自信的，你就会那样行动。

sentences.en: Basically, when you believe I am capable, I am expanding, I am learning, I'm experiencing, I am confident, you act that way.
sentences.zh: 你知道你如何看待自己的处境以及如何看待自己，将影响你身上哪些部分会成长和扩展，哪些部分最终会萎缩。

sentences.en: You know that how you think about your situation and how you think about yourself will influence what parts of yourself grow and expand and what parts ultimately shrink.
sentences.zh: 当然，现实更为微妙。

sentences.en: The reality, of course, is more nuanced.
sentences.zh: 我们已经谈过这一点了。

sentences.en: We've kind of already talked about this.
sentences.zh: 自信是一种技能。

sentences.en: Confidence is a skill.
sentences.zh: 它是源于心态的东西。

sentences.en: It is something that comes from mindset.
sentences.zh: 它不是你与生俱来的，但我们生来就有的其他东西可能会让它变得更难。

sentences.en: It isn't something that you're born with, but there are other things that we are born into that can make it harder.
sentences.zh: 关键在于辨别你的心态何时能胜过那些东西，何时不能。

sentences.en: What it's about discerning is really when your mindset can trump those things and when it cannot.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么拥有一个自信的公式，或者在你的工具箱里拥有技能和东西真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: And that's when having a formula for confidence or having skills and things in like your toolbox really helps.
sentences.zh: 因为与其被情况弄得瘫痪，你确实有选择去尝试，以抵消你缺乏自信、抵消你的焦虑、

sentences.en: Because instead of just feeling paralyzed by situations, you do have options to try out to kind of counteract your lack of confidence, counteract your anxiety,
sentences.zh: 抵消你的社交焦虑、抵消你的冒充者综合症，或者你认为自己不配待在那里的想法。

sentences.en: counteract your social anxiety, counteract your imposter syndrome or your belief that you don't deserve to be there.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实引出了我们今天最大的问题。

sentences.en: So that really leads to the biggest question that we have today.
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么做？

sentences.en: How do we do that?
sentences.zh: 我不会就这样让你们离开而不提供一些实用的建议，包括世界上最自信的人的一些公式，

sentences.en: I'm not just going to leave you guys here without some practical tips, including the formulas
sentences.zh: 如何让你走进任何房间时都感觉棒极了、不可动摇、完全做你自己。

sentences.en: of some of the most confident people in the world, how you can walk into any room feeling amazing, unshakable, completely yourself.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在短暂休息后要探索的内容。

sentences.en: That's what we're going to explore after this short break.
sentences.zh: 自信确实是一场心理游戏。

sentences.en: Confidence is truly a mental game.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，如果你有正确的心理策略，你可以把它们带到任何地方。

sentences.en: And the good thing about that is that if you have the right mental strategies, you can bring these with you everywhere.
sentences.zh: 你可以在任何情况下应用它们。

sentences.en: You can apply them in any situation.
sentences.zh: 如果你的大脑随身携带，这些策略也会随身携带。

sentences.en: If your brain's coming with you, these strategies are coming with you as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想要针对的心态的第一部分，是我们内心深处认为自己根本不配拥有自信的信念，

sentences.en: So the first part of our mindset that we want to target are the deeper beliefs that we have that we don't deserve to be
sentences.zh: 或者认为人们总是能看穿我们。

sentences.en: confident at all, or that people will always be able to see through us.
sentences.zh: 他们总是会把我们看作骗子。

sentences.en: They will always see us as a fraud.
sentences.zh: 他们总是会知道我们在装模作样。

sentences.en: They will always know we're faking it.
sentences.zh: 我们称这些想法，或者至少我称它们为自信阻碍者。

sentences.en: We call these thoughts, or at least I call them confidence blockers.
sentences.zh: 你的想法是你自信和自我信念的强大建筑师。

sentences.en: Your thoughts are powerful architects of your confidence and of your self belief.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实需要你意识到你的自信阻碍者或内心批评者。

sentences.en: So I do need you to become aware of your confidence blockers or your inner critics.
sentences.zh: 当你展示自己或尝试新事物时，你内心批评者最喜欢的口头禅和最喜欢对你说的话是什么？

sentences.en: What is your inner critics' favorite catchphrase and favorite thing to tell you when you're putting yourself out there or trying something new?
sentences.zh: 可能类似于，你做不到这一点。

sentences.en: Probably something along the lines of, you can't do this.
